title: Slowing China Economy Ripples Into Laos
main_content:
A slowing in China’s economy is having rippling effects on Laos, which has been described by the World Bank as having “one of the fastest growing” economies in the East Asia and Pacific region.

A decade long mining boom, combined with a rapid development of hydropower, has seen Laos’ growth rate reach over 7 percent a year, allowing national output to more than double, generating some half a million jobs.

A key player in the economic progress has been China. A recent World Bank report on the Lao economy noted China’s influence was continuing to grow.

China is the leading investor, with $6.7 billion in 760 projects from mining, to energy, agriculture, banking and trade, as well as construction of commercial properties.

In 2015, China accounted for more than 40 percent of Laos’ public external debt, up from 35 percent three years earlier, with the funding focused on infrastructure and power projects.

questions.question: How was Laos described by the World Bank?
options: As having one of the slowest growing economies in the region.
As one of the fastest growing economies in the East Asia and Pacific region.
As a country with declining economic prospects in the forthcoming years.
As economically stable with minimal growth fluctuations.
questions.answer: As one of the fastest growing economies in the East Asia and Pacific region.

questions.question: In which sectors is China described as the leading investor in Laos?
options: Mining, energy, agriculture, banking, trade, and construction of commercial properties.
questions.answer: Mining, energy, agriculture, banking, trade, and construction of commercial properties.
